permission.claude.acceptEdits: File edits and ordinary file actions are approved automatically. Everything else follows the existing CLI rules and a one-time approval.
permission.claude.auto: Claude judges the risk of each action and asks less often. Explicit confirmation rules and protected actions may still need approval. Depending on the model, the provider or an administrator policy it may be unavailable or fall back to manual confirmation.
permission.claude.default: Claude's manual confirmation mode. Reads and previously allowed actions run, and actions that need extra permission ask for a one-time approval.
permission.claude.fullAccess: Ordinary permission checks are skipped. Files and commands outside the project can be reached. Explicit deny rules and the actions the CLI always confirms still apply.
permission.claude.plan: Reads and plans first. It asks for approval before changing sources and applies the CLI's plan mode policy to exploration commands.
permission.codex.acceptEdits: Runs in a sandbox that can write to the working folder. Extra approval requests are not allowed.
permission.codex.default: Runs in a read-only sandbox. Extra approval requests are not allowed.
permission.codex.onRequest: Runs in a working folder sandbox. Commands that need extra permission can be approved once or denied in the app. Allowing network access alone does not guarantee access to keychain credentials.
permission.other.acceptEdits: Uses the CLI's accept-file-edits mode. Other permissions follow the CLI settings.
permission.other.default: Follows the CLI's default permission policy. It can do what the existing CLI settings allow.
permission.other.fullAccess: Runs without approval prompts. It can change files outside the project and run commands.
permission.other.plan: Reads and plans before changing code. It uses the CLI's plan mode.
